The old controller logic had a special case for 'one archetype_id for many decks' (bulk-assign); that path is removed since each deck now has its own named field — bulk assignment from the queue UI wasn't a supported UI gesture anyway.
fix.pr_body:
## Problem

All archetype dropdowns in `/admin/archetypes` shared the same form field name `archetype_id`. When a browser restores a closed tab using "reopen closed tab", it replays the saved form state by field name. If new unassigned decks appeared between close and restore, the browser would apply old selections to the wrong rows — silently misassigning archetypes.

## Fix

**`decksite/views/edit_archetypes.py`**: Set `d['prefix'] = f'{d.id}_'` for each deck in the queue loop. The existing `archetypedropdown.mustache` template already renders `name="{{prefix}}archetype_id"`, so this makes each dropdown uniquely named (e.g. `name="12345_archetype_id"`).

**`decksite/controllers/admin.py`**: Replace the `getlist('archetype_id')` + pop-index approach with a direct per-deck lookup: `request.form.get(f'{deck_id}_archetype_id')` for each `deck_id` in the submitted list. This is simpler and correct — no need for the previous "one archetype for multiple decks" adjustment since each field is now uniquely named.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 848 passed, 1 skipped (environmental skip, unrelated to this change)
- `git diff origin/master...` — 2 files, 7 lines changed; every hunk directly serves #8508

Fixes #8508
